items.title: Core schemas: Rename events + add provider fields
items.description:
Update packages/core/src/schemas.ts to rename Claude-specific event schemas and add provider configuration fields across all relevant schemas. This is the foundational schema change that all other items depend on.

Renames:
- `ClaudeSpawnedSchema` → `LlmSpawnedSchema` (type literal: `claude_spawned` → `llm_spawned`)
- `ClaudeExitedSchema` → `LlmExitedSchema` (type literal: `claude_exited` → `llm_exited`)

New fields on renamed schemas:
- Both `LlmSpawnedSchema` and `LlmExitedSchema` gain `provider: z.string()` (required — identifies which provider ran)

New optional fields on existing schemas:
- `MarkerOptionsSchema`: add `provider?: z.string()`, `providerConfig?: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`
- `BacklogItemSchema`: add `provider?: z.string()`
- `LoopStartOptionsSchema`: add `provider?: z.string()`
- `ToolConfigSchema`: add `defaultProvider?: z.string()`, `providers?: z.record(z.string(), z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()))`

Update `LoopEventSchema` discriminated union to use the renamed schemas. Update all TypeScript type exports (LoopEvent type should reflect the new event names). Update schemas.test.ts to test renamed events and new fields.

items.notes: Reference docs/SPEC-LLM-AGNOSTIC.md §6.2 and §6.3 for exact schema changes. The event rename is a breaking change but acceptable at this stage per §11 risk assessment. The LoopEvent type change will cascade to runner.ts, loop-commands.ts, and loop-manager.ts but those are handled in items 004 and 005.

items.title: Provider types + registry
items.description:
Create the provider adapter type system and factory registry in packages/loop/src/providers/.

New files:

1. `packages/loop/src/providers/types.ts` — All interface definitions:
   - `ProviderId` type alias (string)
   - `LLMProvider` interface: `id`, `displayName`, `execute(prompt, options)`, `checkUsage?()`, `validateCredentials()`, `dispose?()`
   - `ExecuteOptions` interface: `model?`, `timeoutMinutes`, `signal?`, `onProgress?`
   - `ExecutionResult` interface: `stdout`, `stderr`, `exitCode`, `timedOut`, `durationMs`, `parsedSignal?`, `progressEvents?`
   - `ProviderProgressEvent` interface: `type` ('tool_use'|'thinking'|'text'|'error'), `timestamp`, `detail`
   - `UsageLimitResult` interface: `limited`, `limitType?`, `utilization?`, `retryAfter?`, `resetsAt?`
   - Import `Result` type from @ralph/core; import `ParsedSignal` from signal-parser.ts

2. `packages/loop/src/providers/registry.ts` — Provider factory:
   - `registerProvider(id, factory)` — register a provider factory function
   - `createProvider(providerId, config?)` — create provider instance by ID, throws if unknown
   - `getAvailableProviders()` — return array of registered provider IDs
   - Internal Map<string, ProviderFactory> storage
   - ProviderFactory type: `(config?: Record<string, unknown>) => LLMProvider`

3. `packages/loop/src/providers/index.ts` — Barrel export of types and registry functions

Update `packages/loop/src/index.ts` to re-export from providers/.

items.title: Claude CLI provider adapter
items.description:
Create `packages/loop/src/providers/claude-cli.ts` implementing LLMProvider by wrapping the existing Claude-specific code.

This adapter delegates to existing functions — it does NOT rewrite them:
- `execute()` calls `spawnClaude()` from `../claude-process.ts`, mapping its options and result to the provider interface types
- `validateCredentials()` calls `readClaudeOAuthToken()` from `@ralph/core` — returns ok if token readable, err if not
- `checkUsage()` calls `checkUsageLimit()` from `../usage-checker.ts` using the token from `readClaudeOAuthToken()`
- `id` = `'claude-cli'`, `displayName` = `'Claude Code (CLI)'`

Register in the provider registry as the default provider. Registration should happen at module load time (side effect of importing claude-cli.ts), or via an explicit `registerBuiltinProviders()` init function called from the registry module.

The adapter maps between the existing function signatures and the LLMProvider interface:
- `spawnClaude(prompt, { sessionTimeoutMinutes, model, signal })` → `execute(prompt, { timeoutMinutes, model, signal })`
- Return `{ stdout, stderr, exitCode, timedOut, durationMs }` → `ExecutionResult`
- `checkUsageLimit(token)` result → `UsageLimitResult`

items.title: Refactor LoopRunner to use provider interface
items.description:
Modify `packages/loop/src/runner.ts` to use the LLMProvider interface instead of directly calling Claude-specific functions.

Constructor changes:
- Accept optional `LLMProvider` parameter. If not provided, resolve from registry using provider ID from options or default 'claude-cli'
- Store as `this.provider`

Execution changes:
- Replace `spawnClaude(prompt, { sessionTimeoutMinutes, model, signal })` → `this.provider.execute(prompt, { timeoutMinutes, model, signal })`
- Replace `readClaudeOAuthToken()` + `checkUsageLimit(token)` in preflight → `this.provider.checkUsage?.()`
- Add `this.provider.validateCredentials()` call in preflight (before usage check)
- Signal extraction: use `result.parsedSignal ?? parseSignal(result.stdout)` to support both structured and text-based signals
- Call `this.provider.dispose?.()` in finally block

Event changes:
- Emit `llm_spawned` instead of `claude_spawned` (with `provider: this.provider.id` field)
- Emit `llm_exited` instead of `claude_exited` (with `provider: this.provider.id` field)
- Log messages: use `this.provider.displayName` instead of hardcoded 'Claude'

Update runner.test.ts:
- Create a mock LLMProvider for tests instead of mocking spawnClaude directly
- Update event assertions to check for llm_spawned/llm_exited with provider field

Update packages/loop/src/index.ts exports if needed.

items.notes: Reference docs/SPEC-LLM-AGNOSTIC.md §4.4 for the before/after code comparison and §4.5 for the complete mapping table. items.title: Generic CLI provider
items.description:
Create `packages/loop/src/providers/generic-cli.ts` implementing LLMProvider for any user-configured CLI agent.

Configuration via `providerConfig` (from .ralph.json or ~/.ralph/config.json):
- `binary` (required): path or name of the CLI binary to spawn
- `args` (optional): array of argument strings, supporting template variables
- `env` (optional): record of additional environment variables
- `promptDelivery` (optional): 'stdin' (default) | 'file' | 'arg'

Template variables resolved at execution time:
- `{{model}}` → replaced with the model string from ExecuteOptions
- `{{prompt_file}}` → replaced with path to temp file containing the prompt (when promptDelivery is 'file')
- `{{prompt}}` → replaced with the prompt string (when promptDelivery is 'arg')

Prompt delivery modes:
- `stdin` (default): pipe prompt to process stdin, then close stdin
- `file`: write prompt to a temp file, pass path as `{{prompt_file}}` in args, clean up temp file after
- `arg`: pass prompt as `{{prompt}}` in args (for short prompts only)

Process management: use similar spawn/capture/timeout logic as claude-process.ts but with configurable binary and args. Return stdout/stderr/exitCode for standard signal parsing.

`validateCredentials()` checks that the binary exists and is executable (use `which` or `Bun.which`).
`checkUsage()` returns undefined (no built-in rate limit API for generic agents).

Register as 'generic-cli' in the provider registry.

items.title: Claude Agent SDK provider
items.description:
Create `packages/loop/src/providers/claude-sdk.ts` implementing LLMProvider for in-process Claude execution via the Agent SDK.

Dependency:
- Add `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` as optional peer dependency to `packages/loop/package.json`
- Use dynamic import (`await import(...)`) so the package is only loaded when the provider is actually used

Implementation:
- `execute()`: use SDK's `query()` async generator to iterate structured messages
  - Register `ralph_signal` MCP tool that captures structured signals (done/blocked/needs_human + optional reason)
  - Stream progress events via onProgress callback → ProviderProgressEvent (tool_use, thinking, text, error)
  - Collect stdout equivalent from text messages for fallback signal parsing
  - Set `parsedSignal` from MCP tool capture if available
  - Use `permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'` for headless operation

- `validateCredentials()`: check `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var exists and is non-empty; return err if missing
  - MUST NOT accept OAuth tokens (per Anthropic policy — see §9 of spec)

- `checkUsage()`: map SDK 429 errors to UsageLimitResult; no proactive usage API (API key billing is different from subscription)

- `dispose()`: cleanup any SDK resources

Register as 'claude-sdk' in provider registry.

items.title: Gemini CLI provider
items.description:
Create `packages/loop/src/providers/gemini-cli.ts` implementing LLMProvider for the Google Gemini CLI agent.

Provider details:
- `id`: 'gemini-cli'
- `displayName`: 'Google Gemini CLI'
- Binary: `gemini` (spawned as subprocess)
- Headless flags: `--permissive-open` for non-interactive headless operation (per spec), plus research any additional flags needed
- Prompt delivery: stdin or argument (research which gemini CLI supports)

Credentials:
- `validateCredentials()`: check for either `GOOGLE_AI_STUDIO_KEY` env var OR valid Google account auth (check for gcloud credentials file or similar)

Signal parsing:
- Uses standard text parsing from stdout — the RALPH.md prompt instructs the agent to output RALPH_DONE/RALPH_BLOCKED/RALPH_NEEDS_HUMAN

Usage:
- `checkUsage()`: return undefined (no built-in rate limit API check for now)

Process management: spawn gemini binary, capture stdout/stderr, support timeout and AbortSignal cancellation.

Register as 'gemini-cli' in provider registry.
acceptanceCriteria: gemini-cli.ts exports a provider factory implementing LLMProvider
id is 'gemini-cli' and displayName is 'Google Gemini CLI'
execute() spawns 'gemini' binary with --permissive-open and any other headless flags
Prompt delivered to gemini via appropriate mechanism (stdin, arg, or file)
stdout and stderr captured for signal parsing
validateCredentials() checks GOOGLE_AI_STUDIO_KEY env var (or Google account auth); returns err if missing
checkUsage() returns undefined (no rate limit API integration)
Process timeout and AbortSignal cancellation supported
Registered in provider registry as 'gemini-cli'
Unit tests with mock binary verify execute flow, credential validation
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes
items.notes: Reference docs/SPEC-LLM-AGNOSTIC.md §5.4. Similar to the Codex provider — the exact flags may need research at implementation time. The --permissive-open flag is mentioned in the spec as needed for headless operation. Google credential detection may check for GOOGLE_AI_STUDIO_KEY env var first, then fall back to checking if gcloud auth is configured. CLI flags are TBD and require research at implementation time. Evaluate whether this should be a standalone provider or a generic-cli configuration preset — if no custom logic is needed beyond binary+args, prefer generic-cli preset.

items.title: Per-item provider routing
items.description:
Enable per-item provider selection in the loop runner, so different backlog items can execute against different LLM providers within the same loop run.

Runner changes (`packages/loop/src/runner.ts`):
- During each iteration, after selecting the next item, read `item.provider` field
- If `item.provider` is set and differs from current provider, resolve the new provider from registry
- Cache provider instances by ID to avoid recreating them each iteration
- Use the item-specific provider for that iteration's execute() call
- Fall back to the loop's default provider if item.provider is not set
- On loop end, dispose all cached provider instances

The provider resolution for a single iteration becomes:
```
item.provider > loop default provider (from resolution chain in item 007)
```

Integration test: create a backlog with two items specifying different providers (use mock providers), verify both complete with their respective providers.
acceptanceCriteria: Runner reads item.provider field during each iteration
If item.provider is set, resolves that provider from registry for the iteration
Provider instances cached by ID (Map<string, LLMProvider>) — not recreated each iteration
If item.provider is not set, uses the loop's default provider
llm_spawned and llm_exited events for each iteration use the correct provider ID
Log messages use the iteration-specific provider's displayName
All cached provider instances disposed via dispose?.() on loop exit (in finally block)
validateCredentials() called for each unique provider before first use
Integration test: two items with different mock providers complete successfully using their respective providers
Integration test: item without provider field uses default provider
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes
items.notes: Reference docs/SPEC-LLM-AGNOSTIC.md §6.1 for the resolution order (item.provider is highest priority) and §8 Phase 4 tasks. This was originally listed as out of scope in §2.3 but was included in Phase 4 of the implementation plan. The caching is important — creating a new provider instance per iteration would be wasteful, especially for SDK providers that maintain connections. Dependencies relaxed: items 011/012 are nice-to-have for testing but not logically required — routing works with any two registered providers (e.g., claude-cli + generic-cli).
